pr_title: Fix actors getting added to the world improperly updating power state
pr_body: Closes #18454 by implementing the first suggestion of https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/issues/18454#issuecomment-665326254.
pr_comments: Updated with a fix that is more general and should make things a bit more robust in general by not allowing actors which are not in the world to add/update power.

issue_context.title: Going Low Power by building/capturing a building doesn't disable that building.
issue_context.body:
First noticed on RV, can reproduce on RA on bleed too. To reproduce start a game, enabled all cheats, disable unlimited power, build a power plant and build 3 radars, you'll see that the 3rd one won't be disabled.

![resim](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7933210/88661791-c6380300-d0e1-11ea-9713-aef41362e554.png)
comments: Maybe, this started with a recent engine update i did in RV, didn't check what actually regressed it. But that looks like a possible candidate.

This seems to happen because `TraitEnabled` runs before the actor is added to the world. It is then not included in the actors that are set low on power. Three ideas here:
- Don't update the power state from `TraitEnabled` when the actor is not in the world and let the `INotifyAddedToWorld` callback handle it
- Put the update callback in a `FrameEndTask` like we do in `INotifyCreated.Created`
- Set the power state regardless of if the actor is in world or not (probably not that good of an idea, seeing how actors not in the world don't grant or consume power)

review_comments:
_Don't_ remove this actor from the player's power if it _is_ in the world?
Would you explain for me why we want this behavior, please?

This method doesn't remove actors from the world, which means the actor should already be removed from the world when this runs since removing power of an actor that still is in the world is wrong. (The same as adding power of an actor that is not in the world.) I can add a comment to clarify that.

> since removing power of an actor that still is in the world is wrong

One place that calls this method is `Power.OnOwnerChanged`, that's a situation where the actor isn't removed from the world but definitely should be removed from the old owners' PowerManager.

But the actor should be removed from the world before any `OnOwnerChanged` callbacks run: https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/blob/bleed/OpenRA.Game/Actor.cs#L430
Or am I missing something here?
